articleTitle: Some electromagnetic field exposures can have a causal link with cancer and other illnesses
publicationTitle: IEE Half-Day Colloquium on Electro Magnetic Fields - Is the Force with You? (Digest No. 1998/239)
abstract: The author argues that electromagnetic fields (EMFs) can cause cancer by concentrating on those situations where the evidence is strongest; indeed current evidence does not support the blanket argument that all EMF exposure is inherently carcinogenic. He also illustrates that EMF health research is alive and well, and while there remain significant gaps in the scientific knowledge, many new findings continue to be made and new avenues for investigations opened up.

articleTitle: Are low level, low frequency, electromagnetic fields bad for human health?
publicationTitle: IEE Half-Day Colloquium on Electro Magnetic Fields - Is the Force with You? (Digest No. 1998/239)
abstract: Man-made electric and magnetic fields are ubiquitous in developed countries and we are all, to varying degrees, exposed to them in our everyday lives. They come from a variety of sources. At low frequencies the most common source is the electricity supply network (which has a frequency of 50 Hz in the UK and 60 Hz in the USA), and appliances directly powered from it. Here, the author examines whether low level, low frequency, electromagnetic fields are actually bad for human health.
